_comment: Hand-authored. The spawn-script interpreter, bank 7 $F78F-$F85C (its command table $F7C9 is claimed in 73-weapon-tables). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: Spawn-script interpreter: select the script's bank
regions.description: Called from one place, $E998 in the loader/spawn entry $E995 (after the art-load step, with the caller's bank on the stack), once per stage step. $7F = the bank that holds the script: 5 for a labyrinth room's script, 4 for a corridor wave script (stream command 2 sets it). The script pointer is $66/$67 and the wait counter $68; $60 bit 1 = a script is running, bit 3 = spawning is stopped (a boss fight).

regions.name: Interpreter: is it time for a tick?
regions.description: No script running ($60 bit 1 clear) -> return. LABYRINTH ($30 bit 6 clear), or a corridor whose scroll speed $B8/$B9 is 0: $69 is decremented once per call and reaches 0 every 60 calls, so the script advances once a second (frames). A corridor that is scrolling advances once per NEW BACKGROUND ROW instead ($A0 bit 2, set when a row is built and cleared by the next stage step). RUN: a corridor script with no new row never advanced; with a row each call it advanced every call; a stopped corridor counted $69 like the labyrinth. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Interpreter: a tick - count the wait, fetch the next item
regions.description: $69 = 60 for the next second, Y = 0; $68 is decremented and the script returns until it reaches 0 (so a wait of N is N ticks; a wait of 0 wraps to 255 and lasts 256 ticks - RUN). Then the next byte of the script: Y + 1 -> $15 (the offset of its operands); a value under 3 is a command, anything else a spawn (-> $F7F4). RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Command dispatch
regions.description: JSR $D6AE: the inline jump table that follows ($F7C9, three entries): 0 wait, 1 jump, 2 end.

regions.name: Script command 0: wait
regions.description: One operand byte -> $68 (the number of ticks to wait; ticks are seconds in the labyrinth and rows in a scrolling corridor), then $F852 saves the pointer and returns. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Script command 1: jump
regions.description: Two operand bytes (low, high) -> the script pointer $66/$67 and the next item is fetched AT ONCE, in the same tick (Y = 0, JMP $F7BD): a loop with no wait in it would never return, and the five labyrinth scripts that jump into non-script memory carry on reading there. RUN: a one-spawn loop spawned once per tick. RUN with synthetic scripts fed to the real routine through the harness (labyrinth mode, one call per tick).

regions.name: Script command 2: end
regions.description: $60 bit 1 cleared: the script is finished and the routine returns without a tick from then on. RUN: running = 0 from the next call.

regions.name: Spawn item: skip it while spawning is stopped
regions.description: A byte of 3 or more is a type to spawn, $80 and up a FORMATION of the type in its low seven bits. If $60 bit 3 is set (spawning stopped, copied from the boss's $71 at the boss start) nothing is created: a plain type has no operands, a formation's two operand bytes (count, interval) are skipped, and the delay that follows is still honoured. RUN.

regions.name: Spawn item: allocate a slot
regions.description: A plain type takes the LOWEST free slot from 5 up ($FA5B: it only looks, never reclaims; the code switches to bank 6 around the call and back to $7F for no visible reason). A formation uses the allocator $EA8C, which takes the HIGHEST free slot and can reclaim one. If there is no slot the item is dropped exactly as when spawning is stopped (the operands are skipped, the delay honoured). RUN: the first plain spawn went to slot 5, a formation to slot 23; with every slot full both were lost and the script went on.

regions.name: Spawn item: fill the new object
regions.description: A plain spawn stores only the type in $0500,X (the handler sets everything else on its first frame). A formation stores a TYPE-$29 SPAWNER: the formation's type in its metasprite field $0548, the count in $0560 and the interval in $07A0 (read from the two operand bytes), type $29 in $0500; the spawner (bank 6 $9A19) then makes the objects one per interval. RUN: [$91 04 05] gave a $29 object with $0548 = $11, count 4, interval 5.

regions.name: Spawn item: the delay after it
regions.description: The next byte is the DELAY, not a command: a value with bit 7 set is instead the next spawn item (several enemies on the same tick), handled again from $F7F4; otherwise it goes to $68 and the script returns, to act again that many ticks later. A delay of 0 is special: it does not wait, it SKIPS the following byte and carries straight on in the same tick (RUN: the byte after the zero was ignored and the next item spawned on the same tick). No bank 5 script has a zero delay; one bank 4 corridor script has (and one has a wait 0: the tail of corridor 16, see its entry).

regions.name: Interpreter: save the script pointer
regions.description: Adds Y (the bytes read this tick) to $66/$67 and returns; the caller restores the bank.
